gen-dafont-quantum-fs-quicksand: Quantum spaces its letters loosely, with mouths left wide open and ascenders cut short. Quicksand follows with tall, round lowercase bowls and a plain sans line of uniform bars, and that gentle roundness is what sets the pair apart.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-nunito: Contemporary and geometric, Redux spreads its letters wide and sweeps into each curve with a visible entry stroke. And Nunito, a plain sans with big round bowls and terminals held clear of the stem, is the softer partner.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-alpino: Starborn leaves huge gaps between its letters, so each line feels like stars scattered across dark lowercase. Alpino, a tall sans-serif with stubby ascenders and tightly packed spacing, brings the strongest quality here: a cozy, compact counterweight.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-familjen-grotesk: Dreamy gaps stretch between Starborn's letters, with a heavy, dark band of lowercase running through each line. Familjen Grotesk, a lively sans with tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, gives that drifting heading something to land on.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-hind: Starborn scatters its letters across wide, empty gaps. Hind, a sans-serif with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals and strokes steady as drawn string, grounds the pair with quiet, orderly structure.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-nunito: Starborn stretches wide gaps between letters, laying a thick, dark stripe of lowercase across each line. And Nunito, a plain sans with big round bowls and open terminals, would carry a longer read with a soft, friendly ease.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Starborn lays big blank gaps between its letters. Pilcrow Rounded, a plain sans with tall lowercase, big counters and curves left open, is best given a little more size than feels necessary, since its tight spacing needs the room.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-quicksand: Quicksand reads like blown glass bulbs, tall and round, with terminals held clear of every stem. Starborn, dreamy and widely spaced, supplies the dark, heavy lowercase stripe that makes that lightness stand out.
gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-hind: Hind reads steadily, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals and its c never curling inward. Over a long page, Stencilia's structural headings stay striking while that sans keeps going without a wobble.
gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-nunito: Stencilia is structural and striking, with gaps at its curve endings. Nunito, a sans-serif of big round bowls and terminals held clear of the stem, would make a longer read feel soft and welcoming.
